The shift lead reviewed a question about seating plans after a small mix-up
Seating Plan Review and Care Coordination Incident Report

The desk received a routine question from travelers about how seating would align with an animal booking. The matter was handled in the normal customer service flow, with the senior coordinator confirming that the reservation notes were current and that the pet travel details matched the transport plan. During the check, one staff member noticed that the seat preference and the animal placement note had been read together too quickly, which created a brief misunderstanding about where the travelers would sit relative to the pet carrier. No safety concern arose, and the animal remained calm while staff reviewed the file.

The desk welcomed the travelers in a warm, professional tone and explained that the Companion Animal Travel Desk keeps care coordinated from booking through pickup. The staff member then compared the reservation summary with the carrier arrangement and confirmed that the animal, Minnie, was listed correctly for travel. The senior coordinator reviewed the discussion, corrected the seat interpretation, and restated the plan in simple language so the travelers could follow it without stress. The clarification was shared promptly and respectfully, which helped prevent delay and kept the interaction steady.

After the correction, staff checked the boarding notes again to make sure the seating guidance did not conflict with any pet handling step. The travelers were advised that the animal would remain with the approved travel setup and that any further seating questions could be brought to the desk before boarding. The team also noted that the misunderstanding came from a rushed reading of the record rather than from an error in the booking itself. The file was updated with the clarified interpretation so future staff would see the corrected note at once.

Follow-up action was limited to routine monitoring of the record and continued customer contact if needed. The senior coordinator reminded the team to read seating and companion-animal notes separately, especially when a booking contains more than one service detail. No further action was required after the explanation, and the travelers left with a clear understanding of the arrangement. The incident closed normally, and service remained calm throughout.
